why_in_two_sentences: Both competitors are thin: Gottfredson is a short book reflection with a six-item practice list, and the Psychology Today piece is a single-section essay. Ours runs sixteen sections and 34 FAQs, separates composure from departure, and includes a numbered practice protocol plus a specific first-person account of the work.
what_we_do_that_they_dont: Distinguishes real capacity from performed calm (composure vs departure) with physical tells like the chest tightening before going blank
Shows maturity is feeling-specific: someone can be mature about grief and a wreck about anger
Gives an eight-step practice protocol with concrete repetitions (ten extra seconds, the unsent drafted reply)
Includes the author's own multi-year, first-person account of the work, including the domains that have barely moved
34 verbatim FAQs covering intellectualizing, crying at work, humor as avoidance, and the pride of never needing anyone

above_the_fold.ours: H1 is the query, the short answer defines maturity by the ten seconds after something lands, then recognition sentences; earns the scroll.
above_the_fold.theirs: Psychology Today opens with an Esther Perel quote and a PhD byline under a one-line definition; authoritative-looking, but the article beneath is one section long.

trust_signals: Psychology Today shows a PhD author and a named reviewer; Gottfredson is a named author with a book; ours has no byline, though its specific first-person experience account is a provenance signal neither competitor matches.
one_change_with_most_traffic_impact: none - both competitors are materially thinner on definition, mechanism, and practice; optionally add a workplace/leadership FAQ phrasing, the only angle Gottfredson covers that we do not.
